title.en: What Australian law and official guidance say about small businesses using AI
title.zh: 澳洲法律和官方指引对小生意用 AI 怎么说

notes.en: General information with sources, not legal advice. Each record says whether it is quoted from the source or our reading of it (status: confirmed / inference).
notes.zh: 附出处的一般信息，不是法律意见。每条注明是出处原话（confirmed）还是我们的解读（inference）。

summary.en: No Australian law we found requires a small business to have a written AI policy. The government relies on existing, largely technology-neutral laws (privacy, consumer, workplace) rather than AI-specific rules, and its AI guidance is voluntary.
summary.zh: 我们没找到任何澳洲法律要求小生意必须有书面 AI 政策。政府靠现有的、大体技术中立的法律（隐私、消费者、职场）管 AI，不另立 AI 专门规则；官方 AI 指引是自愿的。

sources.quote: The government's regulatory approach to AI will continue to build on Australia's robust existing legal and regulatory frameworks, ensuring that established laws remain the foundation for addressing and mitigating AI-related risks.

summary.en: Most small businesses (annual turnover of A$3 million or less, counting all income from all sources) are not covered by the Privacy Act 1988, but some are.
summary.zh: 大多数小生意（年营业额 A$300 万或以下，所有来源的收入都算）不受《1988 年隐私法》管，但有些例外。

sources.quote: Most small businesses are not covered by the Privacy Act 1988, but some are. A small business is one with an annual turnover of $3 million or less.

summary.en: Whatever their turnover, health service providers are covered by the Privacy Act. This includes medical practitioners, pharmacists, allied health professionals, complementary therapists and child care centres. Also covered regardless of turnover: Commonwealth contractors, credit reporting bodies and AML/CTF reporting entities, among others.
summary.zh: 不论营业额，提供健康服务的都受《隐私法》管，包括医生、药剂师、专职医疗（allied health）、辅助疗法师和托儿所。不论营业额都受管的还有联邦合同承包商、征信机构、反洗钱申报主体等。

sources.quote: traditional health service providers, such as private hospitals, day surgeries, medical practitioners, pharmacists and allied health professionals; complementary therapists; child care centres

summary.en: The OAIC recommends, as best practice, that organisations do not enter personal information, especially sensitive information, into publicly available generative AI tools. Privacy obligations apply to both what goes into an AI system and what comes out of it.
summary.zh: 澳洲信息专员办公室（OAIC）建议，作为最佳做法，不要把个人信息、尤其是敏感信息输入公开的生成式 AI 工具。输入 AI 的和 AI 生成的内容，隐私义务都适用。

sources.quote: As a matter of best practice, the OAIC recommends that organisations do not enter personal information, and particularly sensitive information, into publicly available generative AI tools, due to the significant and complex privacy risks involved.

summary.en: From 10 December 2026, organisations covered by the Privacy Act must say in their privacy policy when a computer program (including generative AI and chatbots) makes or substantially informs decisions that could significantly affect people, and personal information is used. It can apply even when a human reviews the output.
summary.zh: 从 2026 年 12 月 10 日起，受《隐私法》管的机构，如果用电脑程序（包括生成式 AI 和聊天机器人）做出或实质参与可能显著影响个人的决定、并用到个人信息，要在隐私政策里写明。即使有人工复核也可能适用。

sources.quote: On 10 December 2026, APP entities must include information in their privacy policy where they have arranged for a computer program to make or inform decisions that significantly affect individuals' rights or interests.
A decision may be within scope of the transparency obligation even where a computer program output does not replace the entire decision-making process or is subject to human review.

summary.en: The Guidance for AI Adoption (21 October 2025) replaced the 2024 Voluntary AI Safety Standard, condensing 10 guardrails into 6 essential practices: decide who is accountable; understand impacts and plan accordingly; measure and manage risks; share essential information; test and monitor; maintain human control. The 'Foundations' version is for organisations starting to use AI in low-risk ways.
summary.zh: 《AI 采用指引》（2025-10-21）取代了 2024 年的《自愿 AI 安全标准》，把 10 条护栏缩成 6 个基本做法：定谁负责；了解影响并提前打算；衡量和管理风险；分享必要信息；测试和监控；保持人的控制。其中「Foundations」版是给刚开始、低风险用 AI 的机构。

sources.quote: On 21 October 2025, we published the Guidance for AI Adoption, which outlines 6 essential practices for safe and responsible AI governance.
You don't need to do everything at once. Adapt each practice to fit your organisation's size, use cases and risk profile.

summary.en: The National AI Centre publishes a free AI policy guide and template (published 22 April 2026) and an AI register template. It is one generic template written for organisations with committees; there is no official micro-business version. It says a policy should cover what AI can and can't be used for, who approves higher-risk uses, what data staff can put into tools, when staff oversee AI use, how to report issues, and when the policy is reviewed.
summary.zh: 国家 AI 中心免费提供 AI 政策指南和模板（2026-04-22 发布）以及 AI 登记表模板。它是一份通用模板，按有委员会的机构写，没有官方的微型企业版。它说政策应写清：AI 能用和不能用在哪、高风险用途谁批、员工能往工具里放什么数据、什么时候要人盯着、出了问题怎么报、多久复查一次。

sources.quote: what AI can and can't be used for; who approves higher-risk use cases; what data staff can put into tools; when staff need to oversee AI use; how staff should report issues or misuse; when the policy will be reviewed.

summary.en: The Australian Consumer Law's bans on misleading or deceptive conduct apply whatever technology is used, including AI, and a business can breach them even when acting honestly and reasonably. A business is responsible for misleading content its AI produces.
summary.zh: 《澳洲消费者法》禁止误导或欺骗行为，不论用什么技术（包括 AI）都适用；即使诚实、合理行事也可能违反。AI 生成的误导内容，责任在商家。

sources.quote: The provisions of the ACL which prohibit misleading or deceptive conduct and false and misleading representations apply regardless of the technology through which the advertising is used or enabled.

summary.en: Fair Work Act obligations, including the requirement to consult employees in certain circumstances, can be triggered by introducing AI in the workplace.
summary.zh: 《公平工作法》的义务，包括某些情况下要和员工协商，可能因为在工作中引入 AI 而触发。

sources.quote: a range of obligations under the Fair Work Act apply to workplaces including the requirement to consult with employees in certain circumstances which can include the introduction of AI in the workplace.

summary.en: Organisations covered by the Privacy Act must notify affected people and the OAIC when a data breach is likely to cause serious harm, and must take reasonable steps to assess a suspected breach within 30 calendar days. Whether pasting customer data into a public AI tool is itself a notifiable breach is not stated by the OAIC; it depends on the facts.
summary.zh: 受《隐私法》管的机构，数据泄露可能造成严重伤害时，要通知受影响的人和 OAIC；怀疑有泄露，要在 30 个自然日内评估完。把客户资料贴进公开 AI 工具本身算不算要通报的泄露，OAIC 没直接说，要看具体情况。

sources.quote: any organisation or agency the Privacy Act 1988 covers must notify affected individuals and the OAIC when a data breach is likely to result in serious harm

summary.en: The Victorian public sector's generative AI guideline also applies to contractors and consultants with access to public sector information, so a small business supplying a Victorian department may be bound by it.
summary.zh: 维州公共部门的生成式 AI 指引也适用于能接触公共部门信息的承包商和顾问，所以给维州政府部门供货的小生意可能要守它。

sources.quote: The guideline also applies to all employees, contractors, consultants and volunteers engaged directly or indirectly by in-scope organisations with access to public sector information
